scenes.title: Classroom Scene 4 — Objects and Where They Belong
scenes.brief: Functional classroom-object vocabulary and tidy-up/location language.
targetExamples: The pencils are on the table.
The backpack is next to the shelf.
The boxes are in the shelf.
The teddy bear is on top of the shelf.

scenes.title: Classroom Scene 5 — Quiet Corner
scenes.brief: Calm-state language, simple inference and positional description.
targetExamples: The cat is on the beanbag.
The dog is sleeping on the rug.
The rabbit is next to the dog.
The fish bowl is on the shelf.

scenes.title: Classroom Scene 6 — Art Table and What Belongs
scenes.brief: Classroom problem solving, object categories and simple two-step instructions.
targetExamples: The painting is on the table.
The pencils are in the cup.
The paint is on the table.
The football is on the chair.
The football does not belong with the art things.

scenes.title: Classroom Scene 7 — School Routines
scenes.brief: Show several children following everyday classroom routines in one calm scene.
targetExamples: The child is raising a hand.
The child is giving the paper to the teacher.
The child is packing the bag.
The child is putting the book away.
The child is sitting at the desk.

scenes.title: Classroom Scene 8 — Helping and Cleaning Up
scenes.brief: Talk about helping in the classroom, putting things away and solving little problems.
targetExamples: The child is giving the picture to the teacher.
The child is picking up the pencils.
The child is packing the backpack.
The child is putting the book on the shelf.
They are helping in the classroom.

scenes.title: Classroom Scene 9 — End of the School Day
scenes.brief: Use the scene to discuss calm end-of-day routines and what children do before going home.
targetExamples: The teacher is receiving the picture.
The child is packing the backpack.
The child is putting a book away.
The child is waiting near the teacher.
The child is working at the desk.

scenes.brief: Six spatial examples in a classroom: under, on, in, next to, behind and between.
targetExamples: The backpack is under the desk.
The pencil case is on the desk.
The book is in the bag.
The child is next to the teacher.
The chair is behind the desk.
The crayons are between the books.

scenes.brief: Five classroom routines: raising a hand, listening to the teacher, giving paper to the teacher, packing a bag, and sitting ready.
targetExamples: The child is raising a hand.
The child is listening to the teacher.
The child is giving the paper to the teacher.
The child is packing the bag.
The child is ready to work.

scenes.brief: Five children each showing one classroom task: reading, writing, cutting, gluing, and putting a book away.
targetExamples: The child is reading a book.
The child is writing.
The child is cutting the paper.
The child is gluing.
The child is putting the book away.
